claim: LLMs perform substantially worse on 'counterfactual' variants of tasks they solve well by default, even when they pass comprehension checks for the counterfactual rules: e.g., GPT-4 two-digit addition is ~100% in base 10 but 23% in base 9 and 38% in base 11 without CoT (39% / 57% with zero-shot CoT); similar drops across 11 tasks (programming with 1-based indexing, syntax with different word orders, chess with swapped pieces, etc.).

paper.title: Reasoning or Reciting? Exploring the Capabilities and Limitations of Language Models Through Counterfactual Tasks
paper.citation_source: paperclip search (arXiv index) citation field, `paperclip search -s arxiv <title>`; Semantic Scholar API was rate-limited (HTTP 429) throughout this run
paper.s2_batch_record_title: Reasoning or Reciting? Exploring the Capabilities and Limitations of Language Models Through Counterfactual Tasks

experiment.location_in_paper: Sec 2 (framework, counterfactual comprehension check CCC), Sec 3.1 (arithmetic), Sec 4 (Fig 1, Fig 2), App Table 18 (arithmetic numbers)
experiment.task_or_benchmark: 11 tasks: arithmetic (bases 8/9/10/11/16), programming, basic syntax, natural-language logic, spatial reasoning, drawing, music chords/melody, chess, SET game.
experiment.intervention_or_prompts: Default vs counterfactual world specified in the prompt; with/without 'Let's think step by step' (0-CoT); CCC probes (e.g., successor in base 9).
experiment.evaluation_procedure: 1,000 sampled two-digit additions per base (chosen so answers differ from base-10); accuracy; CCC accuracy reported to verify rule understanding.
experiment.main_comparison: Default task vs counterfactual variant under matched difficulty.
experiment.main_result: Table 18, GPT-4 without 0-CoT: base8 82.3, base9 23.4, base10 100.0, base11 38.4, base16 63.0; with 0-CoT: 60.2, 38.6, 98.2, 56.5, 74.0. GPT-3.5 w/o CoT: 8.3, 6.6, 100.0, 3.8, 17.7. Claude v1.3 w/o CoT: 22.3, 0.2, 99.8, 6.6, 32.4. CCC (successor) high for GPT-4 (e.g., 98-100%). Consistent default>counterfactual gaps across tasks (Fig 2).

downstream.title: Evidence from counterfactual tasks supports emergent analogical reasoning in large language models (Webb, Holyoak, Lu)
downstream.summary: Cited in 2411.12580 (read reference). Argues (for letter-string analogies, a different counterfactual paradigm) that failures stem from counting/indexing demands, and GPT-4 with code execution succeeds - a caution for interpreting counterfactual drops as absence of reasoning. Abstract-level only.

downstream.title: MatheMagic: Generating Dynamic Mathematics Benchmarks Robust to Memorization
downstream.summary: Sec 3.1 snippet read: builds test-time counterfactual math tasks with altered arithmetic rules to separate reasoning from memorization, adopting Wu et al.'s paradigm.

downstream.title: Evaluating Large Language Models at Evaluating Instruction Following (LLMBar)
downstream.summary: App F.3 read: reuses counterfactual tasks to test LLM evaluators; reports degraded judgments on counterfactual variants.

downstream_summary: The paradigm is widely adopted, but I did not find a direct re-run of the base-9 arithmetic (or the other 10 tasks) on reasoning models; reasoning models plausibly close much of the gap, making this a good re-test target.
